public_rationale: Harvey’s current documentation supports reliance on third-party models. Harvey and WRITER also disclose specialized training, which makes 'wrapper' an incomplete description if it means little beyond an interface. These examples establish model dependence, but cannot settle the industry-wide generalization.
limitations: The evidence is a small, non-random set of company disclosures.
Earlier research announcements are context, not publication-day outcome evidence.
A strict 'every startup' reading could produce a different result.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: AI startups are basically wrappers for closed or open source models.

statement.excerpt: They’re all basically wrappers for closed or open source models.

our_interpretation: The surrounding paragraph identifies AI application startups buying models from OpenAI and Anthropic as the relevant population.
The ordinary reading is that these businesses primarily supply application layers around other developers’ models. This does not necessarily mean their engineering is trivial.
The claim describes current product architecture. Use the publication-day snapshot, 2026-11-24, because architecture can be documented contemporaneously.
Treat 'all basically' as a broad generalization requiring representative evidence, rather than letting one atypical company settle the entire claim.
criteria.support_condition: Representative technical disclosures show that the relevant startups primarily provide application layers around third-party models.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Representative evidence or substantial counterexamples show that proprietary model development or other independent technology is central to the relevant startups’ products.
